description: The IN alphabet-name phrase of the SPECIAL-NAMES CLASS clause - a COBOL-2002 addition read from the printed formats: §1985:VI.4.5.2 prints CLASS class-name-1 IS {literal-4 [THROUGH literal-5]} ... with no IN phrase, and §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR10 takes a numeric literal as "The ordinal number of a character within the native character set"; the ISO/IEC 1989:2002 format (12.2.6.1) prints [IN alphabet-name-4] and its GR12 takes the ordinal in that alphabet's character set when the phrase is written. At --std 85 the phrase would change the class's members, so it is refused (kb/Work PB5172). Gated in ONE place, VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitClassDefinitionClause, beside the FOR phrase's gate (VCR row 7.52).
display: the IN alphabet-name phrase of the CLASS clause
citation: ISO §2023:12.3.7.2 (the CLASS clause's IN phrase); §1985:VI.4.5.2 prints no IN phrase for CLASS; §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR10
vcr: VCR Table 7 row 7.52 (d) - the CLASS clause's IN phrase, read from the printed formats
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMCLI.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
SPECIAL-NAMES.
    ALPHABET AL IS "Z" "Y"
    CLASS C1 IS 1 THRU 2 IN AL.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC X(2) VALUE "ZY".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    IF W IS C1 DISPLAY "T" END-IF.
    STOP RUN.
